I will plant winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I’m in Quzhou County on the south Hebei plain, and this is still the steadiest way for me to make use of one full year: wheat takes the cool season, maize catches the summer heat and rain. Most of our rain comes in July to September, so maize fits that well, while wheat needs controlled irrigation. I would not spread myself across too many crops this year. At my age, I want a system I know well, can manage with machinery, and can finish on time without making the work too complicated.

I will keep the plan simple and stable. For wheat, I will use an improved local variety, sow evenly, return straw, and use moderate fertilizer instead of pushing too hard with nitrogen. I will irrigate twice, mainly at the key water stages, and keep pesticide sprays to what is needed for disease and aphids. After wheat harvest, I will move straight into summer maize with hybrid seed and direct seeding on time, because timing matters more than fancy changes. Maize will get one irrigation if rainfall is not enough, plus weed and insect control in season. I’m aiming for solid yields with lower waste, not the highest possible input. That matches what has been working in Quzhou’s wheat-maize system and the local push toward higher yield with less excess fertilizer and water. Sources I used: [Ministry of Agriculture on Quzhou crop area and green agriculture](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202107/t20210720_6372348.htm), [China Agricultural University Quzhou station on 2024 wheat-maize results](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html), [MOA case on Quzhou wheat fertilizer reduction](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/bmdt/202203/t20220307_6390769.htm), [Quzhou climate/crop overview](https://www.weather.com.cn/cityintro/101091015.shtml).
